strengths: Comprehensive empirical evaluation spanning 33 model organisms across 7 models and multiple architectures (1B-32B parameters), demonstrating broad applicability of findings
Novel evaluation methodology using LLM-based interpretability agents with quantitative grading, reducing researcher bias and enabling reproducible assessment (91% vs 39% success vs blackbox baseline)
Strong empirical demonstration of detectable activation differences through multiple complementary methods (Patchscope, Logit Lens, steering) with clear visualization in Figure 1
Causal ablation analysis (Figure 7) providing mechanistic evidence linking phenomenon to overfitting on semantically homogeneous data
Important methodological contribution warning interpretability researchers that narrow model organisms may be unrealistic proxies for broader finetuning
Practical mitigation strategy (mixing pretraining data) with transparent analysis of tradeoffs between bias reduction and target objective learning
Extensive supplementary material with detailed prompts, additional experiments, and qualitative examples enhancing reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty—primarily applies existing techniques (Patchscope, Logit Lens, steering) to activation differences rather than introducing new interpretability methods

Causal analysis incompletely supports core overfitting hypothesis: Gemma3 1B shows positive causal effect on pretraining data, contradicting the explanation; authors' resolution ('directions became crucial for computation') is underspecified

Heavy reliance on LLM-based evaluation introduces potential biases: token relevance grading depends on grader model accuracy and predefined frequent token lists; potential circular reasoning in using LLMs to evaluate LLM artifacts

Mitigation approach provides only partial solution: 1:1 mixing ratio causes agent failure; even 1:0.1 ratio degrades target objective learning; alternative approaches (CAFT) show limited effectiveness

Scope limitations for generalization: Domain organisms (D.5) show dramatically reduced bias, suggesting findings may not generalize beyond semantically homogeneous finetuning; paper acknowledges but does not adequately address when conclusions apply

Statistical rigor concerns: agent evaluation based on only 5 runs; D.6.1 shows heavy-tailed distributions indicating occasional lucky runs; no formal significance testing; grading rubrics applied by fallible LLMs
Limited theoretical understanding: why catastrophic forgetting manifests as readable activation biases, and why semantic homogeneity (vs other data properties) is the key factor remain underexplored

Incomplete failure analysis: EM organisms show persistence of misalignment despite mixing (D.4), challenging the overfitting narrative; position selection varies substantially across models with no principled method for novel scenarios

strengths: Clear and important finding that narrow finetuning leaves detectable traces in activation differences with significant implications for model organisms research
Rigorous and comprehensive experimental validation across 33 model organisms spanning 4 families and 7 architectures (1B-32B parameters)
Novel interpretability agent evaluation providing quantitative assessment beyond subjective interpretation, achieving 91% success vs 39% for strong baselines
Solid mechanistic analysis including causal ablations (Figure 7) demonstrating biases help on finetuning data but hurt generalization, with thoughtful connection to catastrophic forgetting
Multiple validation approaches (Patchscope, Logit Lens, steering) consistently point to same conclusions, providing cross-signal agreement
Strong reproducibility through code availability, detailed prompts/rubrics in appendix, and multiple evaluation runs with variance analysis
Principled statistical analysis using Bayesian GLM with credible intervals rather than point estimates
Clear practical implications and actionable warnings for AI safety and interpretability researchers
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty—applies existing techniques (Patchscope, steering) rather than developing new methods; contribution is primarily empirical application

Scope limitations undermine generality claims: domain-adapted models (Section D.5) show nearly absent token relevance and minimal steering effects, questioning how representative synthetic scenarios are
Incomplete mitigation strategy with unresolved trade-offs: mixing pretraining data reduces bias but impairs target objective learning; at 1:1 ratio agents fail to achieve minimum grades
Heavy reliance on LLM-based graders introducing noise; authors acknowledge but don't adequately address this; lacks human validation of grading accuracy
Mechanistic understanding incomplete: catastrophic forgetting connection is suggestive but not rigorously proven; limited investigation of why specific positions carry information
Agent evaluation is derivative of ADL results and shows substantial variance (Figure 16); performance limitations for vision-language models due to text-only interactions
Unclear generalization: primarily tests narrow finetuning with synthetic domains; limited investigation of moderate/realistic finetuning scenarios or very large model scales (>100B)
Statistical concerns: multiple comparisons without correction; some model organisms underrepresented (1 Subliminal, 6 EM); organism selection could bias conclusions
